atoms.b:
History of LGBTQIA+ rights in the USA
The Stonewall Inn is a gay bar in Manhattan, New York City. In the 1960s, when most states still had laws ((criminalising criminalizing)) ((same-sex)) relationships of any kind, gay bars were frequent targets of violent police ((raids)).

atoms.b: In June 1969, during such a raid in the Stonewall Inn, a fight broke out between bar patrons and police officers. This incident garnered a lot of ((public)) attention as well as support for the patrons and other victims of homophobic and ((transphobic)) violence, and ultimately sparked a series of ((protests)) known as the Stonewall Riots.

These riots mark the beginning of the modern movement for ((LGBTQIA+)) rights, which still continues today. Activists coined the ((acronym)) “LGB” in the 1990s, adding more letters to include more identities as time went on.
The label “queer” has historically been used as a ((derogatory)) term, but since the 1980s, people have been reclaiming it as a ((neutral)) umbrella term for all identities within LGBTQIA+.

atoms.b:
The AIDS pandemic
AIDS is a disease that weakens the ((immune_system)) and was first discovered during the ((outbreak)) in the 1980s. Among the groups of people most affected by the disease were gay and ((bisexual)) men, since HIV spreads through bodily fluids and most men did not use protection during intercourse with other men.

Due to a lack of ((education)) about the spread of the virus, many people thought they could become infected simply by being near an HIV-positive person. This resulted in a vast ((increase)) of ((stigma)) surrounding queer men.

In turn, this stigma led to many members of the queer community avoiding HIV tests or treatment out of shame or fear of ((discrimination)). Until the 2020s, ((queer)) men were still banned from donating blood in both the USA and the UK due to ((prejudicial)) associations between them and AIDS.
